thread:
jordan: Heads up — after turning on hyperbatching + int8 on rb-ranker-3b, MRR dropped ~0.03 on prod holdout. NDCG roughly flat. Anyone else seeing this?
lee: Saw similar on staging. Is KV cache enabled? hyperbatch can change token ordering and kvcache warmup.
samir: Yes kvcache=true. Hypothesis: batching merges prefixes and causes cache misses, increasing variance for short queries.
nina: Can we rerun eval with hyperbatching disabled and same queue depth? Compare NDCG/MRR and tail slices.
jordan: I've kicked off two runs: hyper OFF and hyper ON with kvcache_warmup=2. eval-bot will post links when done.
eval-bot: Results uploaded: /runs/3100001111/overview
- run: hyper-off -> MRR 0.412, NDCG@10 0.685
- run: hyper-on  -> MRR 0.389, NDCG@10 0.687
Full csv: /runs/3100001111/compare.csv
samir: That's telling. MRR drop concentrated on short queries (<6 tokens). Could be priming/prefix merging differences.
lee: Also check candidate ordering nondeterminism with int8 kernels. Try seed fix + deterministic kernels.
jordan: Will try: `./eval_runner --model rb-3b-int8 --seed 42 --kernels deterministic --batching hyper`
nina: Also suggest adding a small human-labeled holdout (n~200) to rule out dataset artifact. High precision focus on the tail.
samir: If deterministic kernels help, it's quant instability. If not, hyperbatching policy needs per-request grouping by prefix hash.
lee: :thumbsup: split tasks — Jordan: deterministic run. Samir: short-query slice dive. Nina: curate human-gold holdout.
jordan: Started deterministic run (ETA ~45m), will post results.
eval-bot: Deterministic run finished: /runs/3100001111/det-run
- MRR 0.408, NDCG@10 0.686
- short-query MRR 0.401 (prev 0.372)
samir: So non-deterministic kernels explain much. Remaining delta likely kv cache batching. Next step: try hyperbatch + prefix-grouping config.
nina: I can PR a simple hash-bucket grouping (first 8 tokens) for staging, quick test.
jordan: Good. Reminder: add a short unit test in eval harness that asserts short-query slice MRR doesn't regress >0.02 on new models. Saves cycles.
